author: Ellen Milligan
description: King Charles III gathered leaders of some of the world’s biggest companies to encourage US-UK investment, as he swung through New York as part of a state visit aimed at shoring up ties between the two allies.
title: King Charles Meets CEOs in Bid to Promote US-UK Investment

description: Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Senator Bernie Moreno (R-OH) discuss their bipartisan Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, warning Chinese-made cars pose a "driving surveillance package" risk and could enable espionage or even remote vehicle takeovers. The two also weigh in on the Iran conflict, with Moreno backing the administration's approach and Slotkin calling for greater congressional authorization and oversight of military action and spending. They speak with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Slotkin, Sen. Moreno on China Auto Threat

author: Manuela Tobias
description: Argentina’s Javier Milei emphasized his support for an embattled member of his government, standing proudly by a cabinet chief embroiled in the type of corruption scandal he vowed to eradicate upon taking office.
title: Milei Stands by His Cabinet Chief Amid a Growing Corruption Scandal

author: Keith Naughton
description: Ford Motor Co. is in early discussions with the Trump administration about working on defense projects, Chief Executive Officer Jim Farley said.
title: Ford in Talks With US on Defense-Related Projects, CEO Says

description: Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former Special Assistant to President George W. Bush, says the US should "give it time" for a Strait of Hormuz blockade to pressure Iran economically, even as such efforts "work slowly." He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ex-Bush NSC Official on Iran Blockade

author: Gerry Doyle
description: Top Pentagon officials finally put a price tag on the war in Iran so far during a contentious congressional hearing on Wednesday. Analysts say the $25 billion figure they cited underestimates the total cost by a large amount.
title: Pentagon’s $25 Billion Price Tag for Iran War May Miss Key Costs

author: Andre Loureiro Dias, Franco Dantas
description: Brazil’s Senate rejected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s nominee to fill a vacant seat on Brazil’s Supreme Court, a stinging political setback for the leftist leader as he seeks reelection.
title: Brazil Senate Rejects Lula’s Pick to Join Supreme Court

author: Jeff Mason
description: President Donald Trump said the US is reviewing its troop levels in Germany and will decide shortly whether to reduce that number, escalating tensions between the countries over the war in Iran.
title: Trump Says US Reviewing Germany Troop Levels Amid Iran Tensions

author: Kelcee Griffis, Saijel Kishan
description: The Federal Communications Commission’s decision to accelerate a license review of Walt Disney Co.’s ABC TV stations caught many people in the agency by surprise, laying the foundation for a likely protracted legal battle over a norm-shattering strategy shift.
title: ABC License Renewal Call Surprised FCC Staff and Shattered Norms

author: Daniel Flatley
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Jerome Powell for his decision to stay on the Federal Reserve Board after he steps down as the US central bank’s chair, saying it amounts to a break with Fed tradition.
title: Bessent Says Powell Staying On Is ‘Violation’ of All Fed Norms

author: Gerry Doyle
description: US Central Command has asked to send the Army’s long-delayed Dark Eagle hypersonic missile to the Middle East for possible use against Iran, seeking a longer-range system to hit ballistic-missile launchers deep inside the country.
title: US Seeks to Deploy Hypersonic Missile for the First Time Against Iran

description: Four tech giants beat analyst estimates as Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft reported earnings after the bell, exposing a significant share of the market as traders reacted. Bloombeg's Ed Ludlow and Anurag Rana, along with Ron Westfall, HyperFRAME Research Infrastructure and Networking VP & practice leader, gave their initial reaction to the reports Meta shares fell in the immediate aftermarket after the company told investors it was increasing its capex for the year, citing rising AI investment costs. While Microsoft's cloud business narrowly beat estimates, it was not enough to ease concerns around its artificial intelligence strategy, as investors fear its not doing enough to capitalize on the AI market.  Alphabet beat estimates across the board, with results spurred particularly by strong growth in its cloud computing unit.  Amazon reported the largest cloud sales growth since 2022, bolstered by deals with Anthropic and OpenAI.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Barrage of Big Tech Earnings Beat Estimates to Mixed Reaction

author: Charles Gorrivan
description: The US is seeking forfeiture of two Iran-linked oil tankers seized by naval forces enforcing a blockade against the Islamic Republic, according to a senior White House official.
title: US Seeks Forfeiture of Iran-Linked Oil Tankers Seized at Sea

author: Nancy Cook
description: The decision is likely to extend battles over redistricting for years.
title: Supreme Court Decision on Minority Districts Will Have a Long Tail

author: Gregory Korte
description: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 was a landmark law enacted to enforce voting protections enshrined in the US Constitution and eliminate longstanding obstacles to voter participation. In recent years, the Supreme Court’s conservative majority has repeatedly narrowed the scope of the 61-year-old law. On April 29, the court limited the use of the law to create predominantly Black or Hispanic election districts — its most important remaining component.
title: What the Supreme Court Ruling Means for Race-Based Voting Districts

author: Roxana Tiron, Courtney McBride
description: Pentagon officials confirmed the release of $400 million in funds for Ukraine that already had been authorized by Congress, after the top Senate Republican overseeing defense spending criticized Pentagon leaders for withholding the money.
title: Pentagon ‘Released’ $400 Million Ukraine Funding, Hegseth Says

author: Chris Strohm, Jimmy Jenkins
description: Former FBI Director James Comey made his initial court appearance Wednesday in response to federal criminal charges for allegedly threatening President Donald Trump’s life in a social media post.
title: Former FBI Director Appears in Court for Second Indictment

author: Chris Dolmetsch, Alex Vasquez, Gonzalo Soto
description: The governor of the Mexican state of Sinaloa and a number of other current and former officials were accused by US prosecutors with conspiring with cartel leaders to import drugs into the US in exchange for political support and bribes.
title: Mexico’s Sinaloa Governor Is Indicted in US on Drug Charges

author: Zoe Tillman, Greg Stohr
description: The Trump administration told a divided US Supreme Court that past remarks by the president disparaging Haiti and immigrants weren’t racist and shouldn’t get in the way of the government stripping temporary protections for migrants.
title: Supreme Court Told Trump’s End to Migrant Shield Not Driven by Race

description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell says he'll continue to serve as a governor “for a period of time to be determined” but with a low profile. He speaks in Washington after the FOMC left interest rates unchanged.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Powell Says He'll Continue to Serve as Fed Governor, But With a 'Low Profile'

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: US President Donald Trump said the United Arab Emirates’ decision to leave OPEC would help lower energy prices, which have spiked due to the war in Iran and continue to climb.
title: Trump Argues UAE’s OPEC Exit Could Lower Energy Prices Amid War

author: Brian Platt, Laura Dhillon Kane
description: South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean Co. said it will partner with Canadian auto parts firms to build armored vehicles if it wins a contract to build a new submarine fleet for Canada.
title: Hanwha to Build Armored Vehicles in Canada if It Wins Submarine Contract

author: Michelle Kaske
description: Labor negotiations between New York City’s transit agency and Long Island Rail Road workers spontaneously kicked off on Wednesday, after a union leader spoke out at a board meeting.
title: NY’s MTA Holds Impromptu Talks With Rail Unions as Strike Looms

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power,  Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses a key Senate committee vote to advance Trump's nominee for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh ahead of Jerome Powell's last fed decision in his role as chair. On today's show, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Partner at Stonecourt Capital Rick Davis, and Republican Senator from West Virginia Shelley Moore Capito. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Chair Nominee Warsh Wins Key Senate Committee Vote | Balance of Power: Early Edition 4/29/2026

author: Anthony Halpin
description: US President Donald Trump said he encouraged Vladimir Putin to conclude his war in Ukraine and rebuffed an offer from his Russian counterpart to help secure Iran’s nuclear material.
title: Trump Presses Putin on Ukraine Deal, Rebuffs Iran Nuclear Offer

author: Allyson Versprille, Joe Lovinger
description: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy floated the idea of charging a fee to help the US Federal Aviation Administration modernize its air traffic control system on a more regular basis.
title: DOT’s Duffy Pitches Fee to Help Pay for Air Traffic Upgrades

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: Texas Democrat James Talarico holds leads over both Republicans vying for the competitive US Senate seat, reflecting voters’ surging concerns about the cost of living and dimming views of President Donald Trump’s handling of the economy, according to a new poll by the University of Texas.
title: Texas Democrat Talarico Has Edge on Republicans in Senate Race

author: Jan Bratanic
description: Slovenia’s nationalist leader and ally of US President Donald Trump inched closer to his political comeback after a vote showed he now commands a majority in parliament.
title: Trump Ally Nearer to Comeback in Slovenia After Vote on Cabinet

author: Enda Curran, Jonnelle Marte
description: Kevin Warsh, President Donald Trump’s nominee to be the next chair of the Federal Reserve, denied connections to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein after his name was referenced in files on Epstein published by the Department of Justice.
title: Warsh Denies Any Connections to Epstein in Response to Warren

author: Jim Wyss
description: Cuba’s top diplomat accused Washington of trying to manufacture a pretext for toppling the government in Havana after US senators failed to limit Donald Trump’s ability to use military force against the island.
title: Cuba Says It Poses No Threat as Rubio Warns of Foreign Influence

author: Kate Sullivan, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump told Axios he will not lift a naval blockade of Iran’s ports until he secures a deal with Tehran to address the country’s nuclear program, extending a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz that has caused a global energy crisis.
title: Trump Says He Rejects Iran Hormuz Offer, Keeps Blockade

author: Samy Adghirni, Magdalena Del Valle
description: The United Nations must deal with its shrinking budget and narrow the scope of its mission, a leading contender for the UN secretary general job said as the US has yet to back a candidate.
title: UN Must Do Less With Less, Says Candidate to Become Next Leader

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump discussed steps the US could take to prolong its blockade of Iran during a meeting with oil and trading industry executives Tuesday, as the Middle East war continues to drive up prices for crude and other commodities.
title: Trump Discussed Extended Blockade With Oil, Commodities Chiefs

description: Kevin Warsh won the backing of the Senate Banking Committee on a 13-11 party-line vote to be the next chair of the Federal Reserve. Mike McKee reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Warsh Wins Key Senate Committee Vote to Be Next Fed Chair

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The man charged with attempting to assassinate Donald Trump at a Washington hotel on Saturday followed the president’s movements in real-time using a website and live video feeds just before a shootout with security at the venue, according to new details disclosed by the US Justice Department.
title: DC Gala Shooting Suspect Tracked Trump’s Movements, DOJ Says

author: Denis Chabrol
description: A tiny brooch worn by Venezuela’s new US-supported leader Delcy Rodríguez has become a diplomatic lightning rod.
title: A Tiny Pin Stokes High-Stakes Dispute Between Venezuela, Guyana

author: Anna J Kaiser
description: Florida’s House on Wednesday backed Governor Ron DeSantis’ bid to redraw the state’s congressional districts in an effort to secure as many as four additional US House seats for Republicans in November’s midterm elections.
title: Florida House Backs DeSantis Bid to Redraw Congressional Lines

description: The US Supreme Court voted 6-3 along ideological lines to limit the use of the Voting Rights Act to create predominantly Black or Hispanic election districts. The justices rejected a Louisiana congressional map that was drawn with a second majority-Black district after a lower court found an earlier map to be discriminatory. Michael McKee reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Supreme Court Limits Use of Race in Drawing Voting Districts

author: Courtney McBride, Roxana Tiron
description: The US has spent an estimated $25 billion on the Iran war so far, the Pentagon comptroller said, providing the most complete public estimate of the conflict’s cost.
title: US Has Spent $25 Billion on Iran Conflict So Far, Pentagon Says

description: Aftab Pureval, mayor of Cincinnati, Ohio, talks about his priorities, adding new housing and rebuilding the waterfront on the Ohio River. He speaks to Bloomberg's Chad Thomas from the Bloomberg CityLab event in Madrid. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Cincinnati Mayor on Infrastructure, Housing, Rebuilding Waterfront

author: Katarina Hoije
description: France urged its citizens to leave Mali “as soon as possible” as a separatist group vowed to expand its campaign to oust the nation’s military junta and Islamist militants renewed a threat to blockade the capital.
title: France Urges Citizens to Leave Mali as Rebels Vow to Oust Junta

author: Galit Altstein
description: Israel is preparing to sell a stake of as much as 30% in its two largest defense companies this year to help fund the nation’s expanding military spending.
title: Israel Readies Sale of Stakes in State Defense Firms by Year-End

author: Patrick Sykes
description: Iran’s currency has fallen in recent days to a fresh record low, in a sign the US’s naval blockade is squeezing the Islamic Republic’s economy.
title: US Naval Blockade Pushes Iran’s Currency to Record Low

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Rajesh Roy
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is poised to secure a landmark victory in West Bengal state for the first time ever, exit polls showed, reinforcing his standing as the country’s most popular political leader.
title: Modi Set to Secure Landmark Win in West Bengal, Exit Polls Show

description:
The US Supreme Court limited the use of the Voting Rights Act to create predominantly Black or Hispanic election districts in a major constitutional ruling that buttresses Republican efforts to keep control of the House in this year’s midterms and beyond.
Voting 6-3 along ideological lines, the justices rejected a Louisiana congressional map that was drawn with a second majority-Black district after a lower court found an earlier map to be discriminatory.
Bloomberg Law Host June Grasso discusses the ruling with Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu on Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Supreme Court Curbs Use of Race in Drawing Voting Districts

author: Steven T. Dennis, Enda Curran
description: Kevin Warsh, President Donald Trump’s nominee to be the next chair of the Federal Reserve, won the backing of the Senate Banking Committee Wednesday on a 13-11 party-line vote, putting him on track to be confirmed by the full Senate before Jerome Powell’s term ends May 15.
title: Fed Chair Pick Kevin Warsh Wins Key Senate Committee Vote

author: Courtney McBride
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US will help allies that step up on defense and punish partners that fail to do so, striking a combative tone as he appeared before Congress on Wednesday.
title: Allies Will ‘Face Consequences’ for Not Helping US, Hegseth Says

author: Martin Z Braun
description: New York City taxpayers may face a bill of more than $500 million next year if proposals to increase public employee benefits are approved as part of the state budget.
title: NYC Taxpayers Face $500 Million Bill Under Pension Proposals

author: Colum Murphy, James Mayger
description: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong delivered a strong message to China on Wednesday: stable shipments of commodities and food requires continued imports of petrol, jet fuel and fertilizer.
title: Australia Tells China Stable Trade Needs Stable Fuel Supply

description: Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham discusses the UK local elections, the threat to Labour posed by the Green Party and Nigel Farage's Reform, and why he thinks Prime Minister Keir Starmer deserves more credit. He talks with Francine Lacqua at Bloomberg's CityLab event in Madrid. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Burnham Sees 'Challenging' UK Local Elections for Labour

author: Jonathan Tirone, Annmarie Hordern
description: Iran could access its stockpile of near weapons-grade uranium if it decides to retrieve the material thought to be entombed at sites bombed by the US, according to the nuclear watchdog of the United Nations.
title: Iran Could Access Uranium Stockpile, Nuclear Watchdog Says

description: International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi says it's believed that Iran's uranium stockpile remains buried at Isfahan. He says as part of any deal, inspectors must be allowed to verify Iran's claims. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: IAEA Believes It Knows Where Iran's Buried Uranium Is

author: Daniel Basteiro, Francine Lacqua
description: Spain should retain a seat on the European Central Bank Executive Board in next year’s reshuffle, the country’s economy minister said, while rejecting the notion he might want the role for himself.
title: Cuerpo Says Spain Wants ECB Board Seat, But It Won’t Be for Him

author: Joe Mayes
description: Nigel Farage was accused by the governing Labour Party and opposition Conservatives of breaking parliamentary rules after the leader of the poll-leading Reform UK acknowledged receiving a large private donation from the crypto investor Christopher Harborne.
title: Farage Accused of Breaking Rules Over £5 Million Donation

description: Apple CEO Tim Cook, pro golfer Rory McIlroy and US Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh were among the guests who attended the state banquet for King Charles in Washington. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Who Attended the State Dinner With King Charles

author: Sam Dagher, Fiona MacDonald, Salma El Wardany, Mirette Magdy
description: The United Arab Emirates’ worsening rift with Saudi Arabia was at the heart of its shock decision to quit OPEC.
title: UAE Bristled at Saudis for Years Before Iran War Tipped Scales

author: Upmanyu Trivedi
description: A person who communicated in Russian and used the pseudonym “El Money” promised to pay alleged arsonists to light a series of fires that targeted property linked to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer last year, prosecutors said at the start of a London trial.
title: Russian Speaking ‘El Money’ Recruited Arsonists to Target Starmer, Prosecutors Say

author: Bonolo Mokonoto
description: Kémi Séba, a French-born influencer wanted by the authorities in Benin in connection with an attempted coup in December, requested bail from a court in South Africa, where he’s accused of trying to exit the country illegally.
title: Fugitive Linked to Benin Coup Bid Seeks Bail in South Africa

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Hearing will be first public questioning by Congress
title: Hegseth to Defend $1.5 Trillion Budget, Iran War at Hearing

author: Ignacio Olivera Doll
description: Concern is mounting once again in the bond market that Argentines are tiring of President Javier Milei and his radical economic reform agenda.
title: Argentina Bond Investors Increasingly Fear the Day After Milei

description: Daniel Werfel, former Commissioner of the US Internal Revenue Service, joined Caroline Hepker and Lizzy Burden on Bloomberg Radio as the UK's tax authority undertakes a major digital overhaul. HMRC is aiming to move most customer interactions online by 2030, while updating legacy systems and exploring the use of AI. Werfel, now with Public Digital, which is advising HMRC, discussed the challenges of delivering large-scale government transformation, as well as concerns around AI, data protection and the security of sensitive public sector systems. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: AI Presents 'Unique Risks' Warns Former IRS Chief

author: Upmanyu Trivedi
description: Mercedes-Benz Group AG’s financial services unit filed an appeal challenging the UK’s £7.5 billion plan to compensate customers who were overcharged for auto loans.
title: Mercedes Set to Challenge UK’s £7.5 Billion Motor Finance Plan

author: Jenny Leonard, Yian Lee, Cindy Wang
description: Germany and the Czech Republic denied requests for Taiwan President Lai Ching-te to transit through Europe earlier this month, dooming his last-minute effort to circumvent a China-backed blockade of his first diplomatic trip to Africa, people familiar with the matter said.
title: Taiwan Leader’s Last-Minute Plea to Fly Via Europe Was Rejected

author: Jon Herskovitz
description: Kim Jong Un has shown no sign that the US president can entice him to abandon nuclear ambitions.
title: North Korea Nuclear Arms Shield Kim From Trump

author: Daniel Hornak
description: Slovakia’s Supreme Court upheld a 21-year prison sentence for Juraj Cintula for the attempted assassination of Prime Minister Robert Fico, ruling the act a terrorist attack, Slovak TASR news agency reports.
title: Slovak Premier Fico Attacker Sentenced to 21 Years, TASR Says

description: Federal Reserve officials are expected to leave interest rates unchanged on Wednesday, holding the benchmark rate in a range of 3.5% to 3.75% for a third consecutive meeting. Investors will be looking for clues about how long the Fed is willing to maintain its patient posture, as well as what Chair Jerome Powell says about his future at the central bank. Bloomberg's Jill Disis reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Federal Reserve Expected to Hold Rates

author: Arne Delfs
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s cabinet approved a healthcare overhaul and a multi-year budget blueprint, laying the groundwork for a push to revive Germany’s economic growth.
title: German Coalition Clears Crucial Healthcare, Budget Packages

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat
description: Former Thai premier Thaksin Shinawatra will be released on parole after serving eight months in jail, paving the way for his possible return to politics as his family’s party takes a lesser role in a new conservative-led government.
title: Ex-Thai PM Thaksin Set for Parole After Eight Months in Prison

author: Alex Chapman
description: Australia’s richest person, Gina Rinehart, has donated a plane to Pauline Hanson, the leader of the country’s hard-right One Nation Party.
title: Australia’s Richest Gifts Jet to Hard-Right Party Head

description: President Donald Trump, in a post on Truth Social, said Iran doesn’t “know how to sign a nonnuclear deal” and needs to “get smart soon.” His comments come after the US signaled it would stick with a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz as it tries to choke off Tehran’s oil exports and force it back to the negotiating table. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran ‘Better Get Smart Soon’

author: Caitlin Reilly, Steven T. Dennis
description: Republican lawmakers are looking at ways to lower taxes on capital gains as the party searches for new ways to woo voters worried about the cost of living heading into November’s midterm elections.
title: Republicans Eye Capital Gains Tax Cut to Ease Voters’ Anxieties

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: The impeachment effort against Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte was advanced by a key congressional panel, paving the way for further battles over a politician who aims to be a contender in 2028’s presidential election.
title: Philippine Panel Finds Probable Cause to Impeach VP Duterte

author: David Herbling
description: The war in Iran is fueling a resurgence in maritime piracy off the coast of Somalia, according to a European Union naval force patrolling the region.
title: Iran War Fuels Piracy Surge Off Somalia Coast, EU Agency Says

author: Daniel Basteiro, Francine Lacqua
description: Cities are increasing investment in the green transition to protect against the potentially catastrophic effects of climate change, the European Investment Bank president said.
title: Cities Need to Boost Green Investment for Safety, EIB Chief Says

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union warned the continent may spend years grappling with fallout from the US-Israeli war in Iran, signaling that an energy price spike will not abate soon.
title: Von der Leyen Warns Iran War May Damage Europe for Years

description: The US signaled there will be no letup with its naval blockade of Iranian ports, as it tries to choke-off Tehran’s oil exports and force it back to the negotiating table. The blockade lies at the heart of the impasse between the US and Iran, with the Islamic Republic insisting it won’t restart negotiations or reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the naval restrictions stay in place. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Signals It Will Stick With Hormuz Naval Blockade

author: Michael Nienaber
description: Donald Trump attacked Germany’s Friedrich Merz after the chancellor criticized the US handling of its war on Iran.
title: Trump Says Germany’s Merz ‘Doesn’t Know What He’s Talking About’

author: Gian Volpicelli
description: The European Union’s executive arm accused Meta Platforms Inc. of failing to keep young children off its services, ramping up a probe that could result in hefty fines.
title: EU Escalates Probe Into Meta for Failing to Stop Kids Signing Up

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Russia will stage its traditional May 9 parade marking the defeat of Nazi Germany in World War II without heavy military equipment for the first time since 2007, as the war in Ukraine takes its toll on President Vladimir Putin’s army.
title: Russia Cuts Tanks, Missiles From Putin’s WWII Parade in First Since 2007

author: Omar Tamo, Arsalan Shahla
description: The US signaled it would stick with a naval blockade of Iranian ports, as it tries to choke-off Tehran’s oil exports and force it back to the negotiating table.
title: US Signals No Letup of Naval Blockade as It Aims to Squeeze Iran

description: Mali’s leadership signaled it will not rethink its Russia-backed security strategy, even as the scale of rebel attacks over the weekend raises fresh questions over its effectiveness. Insurgents recaptured the Malian town of Kidal, a town that Kremlin-linked fighters wrested back in 2023. Africa Corps, a force overseen by Russia’s defense ministry, announced it was withdrawing from Kidal. The pullback punctures the claim that Moscow could deliver where France and other Western allies could not. Bloomberg's Jennifer Zabasajja reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Mali Reaffirms Russia Ties After Major Jihadist Assault

author: Thomas Escritt, Jorge Valero
description: Hungary’s incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar will push for a deal to restore access to billion of euros in frozen European Union aid during the first trip to Brussels since his landslide election victory two weeks ago.
title: Hungary’s Magyar Is Pushing for Rapid Access to Billions From EU

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi, Jorge Valero
description: The European Union is considering imposing stricter conditions on its €90 billion ($105 billion) loan to Ukraine, making some of the payouts dependent on the introduction of an unpopular tax change for businesses, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Ukraine Faces Risk of Tougher EU Loan Terms to Get Aid Payouts

author: Brendan Scott
description: In one legislative chamber, a British king appealed to centuries of shared history in a bid to preserve his country’s most important alliance. In another, an ocean away, a British prime minister watched his agenda get sidelined again by his past efforts to protect the US-UK “special relationship.”
title: UK’s Split-Screen Moment Lays Bare Struggle to Adapt to Trump

author: Philip Heijmans
description: Vietnam’s General Secretary and President To Lam will deliver the keynote address at Asia’s top security summit this year, giving the Southeast Asian leader a high-profile opportunity to address long-standing territorial tensions with Beijing in the South China Sea.
title: Vietnam’s To Lam to Give Keynote Speech at Asian Defense Forum

author: Nectar Gan, Rebecca Choong Wilkins, Colum Murphy
description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are headed toward a summit next month with a shared desire to stabilize ties. That calm is being tested as both leaders rush to shore up strategic vulnerabilities over Iranian oil and AI.
title: China, US Tensions Build Over Iran and AI Before Trump Meets Xi

author: Echo Wong, Zheping Huang, Haze Fan
description: The AI startup Manus, once hailed as a breakthrough that would challenge Silicon Valley’s dominance, is turning into a cautionary tale for Chinese entrepreneurs after Beijing authorities ordered Meta Platforms Inc. to unwind its $2 billion takeover of the company.
title: China’s Meta Backlash Renders Manus Model ‘Officially Dead’

author: Andreo Calonzo
description: The Philippine tax agency has ordered tax audits on nine businesses tied to Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband.
title: Philippine Tax Agency Orders Probe on VP Duterte’s Businesses

author: Malcolm Scott
description: China’s dominance of rare earths supply chains gives President Xi Jinping economic leverage worth $1.2 trillion in his planned summit meeting with US President Donald Trump in Beijing next month.
title: Xi Has $1.2 Trillion Rare Earths Leverage Ahead of Trump Visit

author: Rajesh Roy
description: Millions of voters in India’s eastern state of West Bengal head to the polls on Wednesday in the final phase of a key local election, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeks to win there for the first time.
title: Modi Seeks First Win in West Bengal With Voting in Final Phase

author: Soma Biswas, Ryan Gould, Reshmi Basu
description: Talks over a potential $500 million US government rescue financing deal for Spirit Aviation Holdings Inc. have hit an impasse, with a lender group that includes Citadel, resisting terms that would likely severely impair their claims and recoveries, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Some Spirit Lenders Balk as US Rescue Talks Hit Impasse

author: John Harney
description: President Donald Trump has nominated G. Hunter McMaster II to be assistant Treasury secretary for Financial Markets, though he has been performing the duties of that post since last July.
title: Trump Nominates Ex-Bessent Hedge Fund Executive to Treasury Post
